chapters.title: When KQL is the right tool

takeaways: KQL databases in Fabric live inside eventhouses in a workspace and are built for append-only event and time series data, not transactional records.
KQL queries read top to bottom through pipes, using take, project, where, extend, summarize, bin and render to turn raw events into answers.
Before going live, decide on retention, permissions, table ownership and alert destinations so insights reach someone who can act.
hook: Teams collect endless alerts, clicks and device signals yet still miss the change that mattered. This episode explains KQL databases in Microsoft Fabric for beginners and SQL users alike, from eventhouses and event streams to the handful of KQL operators that turn event noise into timely action.
